image_description: A vintage black typewriter viewed from the front. The image focuses on the keyboard area, specifically highlighting the long, horizontal key at the bottom center (the space bar). The keys are round with metallic or white tops. There is visible wear and dust on the machine. Faint, possibly gibberish text or symbols are visible on the front panel below the space bar.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is elongated, but it does NOT span the 'full width' of the bottom row. It is centrally positioned with significant gaps/other structural elements to its left and right. The checkpoint description implies a modern keyboard layout where the space bar is the widest key spanning nearly the whole width, whereas this vintage typewriter has a shorter space bar relative to the total machine width.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is wider than the circular type keys, but not 'dramatically' so in the sense of modern keyboards (10x). It appears to be roughly 4-5 times the diameter of a single round key. The proportion is inconsistent with the specific '10x' claim in the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is flat or slightly concave.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top surface of the space bar appears relatively flat, consistent with vintage typewriter designs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside and internal mechanical linkages (stabilizer bars) are completely occluded by the keycap and the camera angle. Impossible to verify visually.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label is typically blank with no printed character.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top surface of the space bar is black and shows no printed letters or symbols, matching the 'blank' criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Positioned centrally between modifier keys on the bottom row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is clearly centered at the bottom of the key arrangement. While 'modifier keys' (Shift/Ctrl) are not explicitly distinct in this vintage layout, it is centrally positioned between the ends of the key block.

The material appears to be aged metal or hard rubber/bakelite with a semi-gloss or worn finish, not the smooth matte plastic typical of modern computer keyboards. There is visible texture from wear and dust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Typically white, black, or gray to match keyboard color scheme.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is black, matching the rest of the typewriter's body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Part of a standard computer or typewriter keyboard.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly part of a vintage typewriter keyboard.

artifact_observations.location: Front panel below the space bar
artifact_observations.reasoning: There are faint, indistinct markings or symbols on the front face of the typewriter body below the space bar. They resemble degraded text or AI-generated gibberish rather than clear branding or model numbers. This is a common artifact in AI generations of objects with text.

The texture on the round keys and the body has a slightly 'smudged' or overly uniform noise pattern that lacks the crisp micro-scratches and dust distribution of a real macro photograph. It looks slightly painterly.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the keyboard deck
artifact_observations.reasoning: The alignment of the keys on the far right becomes slightly irregular and less defined compared to the left side, suggesting minor geometric instability or melting in the generation process.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mismatch between the Taxonomy Prior Knowledge (which describes a modern computer space bar: 'spanning full width', '10x width') and the actual image (a vintage typewriter space bar). The Router marked several geometry checkpoints as 'false' because of this mismatch. Determine if this constitutes an 'alignment failure' (wrong type of space bar generated) or if the 'space bar' class is broad enough to include typewriters. Also, scrutinize the 'text_gibberish' artifact; if the text is illegible, it significantly impacts the artifact score. Do not let the 'vintage aesthetic' excuse structural sloppiness in the key alignment.
